cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

mechanism: A protects a pupil from a painful rejection by reframing failure as achievement in a different lesson it claims to have taught.
confusable: The lie is meant to preserve B confidence, not merely hide A responsibility or seek praise for teaching.
comparison: Bakery rejection managed through a display pretext versus a rejected poet seeking public endorsement.
seedUse: D15 inedible letter/display alternative establishes the protected truth; S05 claims instruction in the substitute achievement.
